title: VDC System Deactivated (ECM Signal Interruption)
meaning: Vehicle Dynamics Control (VDC / ABS 7D0) detected that the Engine ECM has disabled engine torque modulation due to an active engine diagnostic trouble code.
symptoms: VDC / Traction light illuminated
Cruise Control light flashing
Eyesight pre-collision braking disabled
inspectionSteps: Do NOT replace VDC module, ABS sensors, or brake booster for C0057. C0057 is a companion fault.
Scan Engine ECM (7E0) for primary DTC (e.g. P0420, P0011, P0325, misfire).
verifiedFixes: Diagnose and repair primary engine fault code in ECM.
Clear codes across all modules with OBD-Hero multi-ECU clear function.

title: Intake Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
meaning: ECM commanded variable valve timing (AVCS) retard, but camshaft position sensor detected the intake camshaft remained mechanically advanced beyond calibrated limits.
symptoms: Check Engine Light illuminated
Cruise Control light flashing / Eyesight disabled
Rough idle and loss of low-end torque
Engine stall when coming to a stop
inspectionSteps: Check engine oil level and condition: dirty or low oil is the primary root cause of AVCS hydraulic lag.
Remove and inspect AVCS oil feed line banjo bolt on passenger cylinder head: the tiny internal mesh screen filter clogs with carbon/sludge (Subaru TSB 02-106-08).
Remove Bank 1 Oil Control Valve (OCV) on front of head: test 12V actuation and inspect spool plunger for sticking varnish.
Check live data: VVT Advance Angle actual vs target (should track within 2 degrees of target).
verifiedFixes: Remove and permanently discard the micro mesh screen filter inside the cylinder head turbo/AVCS oil supply banjo bolt (official Subaru revised technical service bulletin recommendation).
Replace Bank 1 AVCS Oil Control Valve (OCV) solenoid (OEM Subaru 10921AA040 or equivalent).
Perform engine oil flush and install genuine OEM Subaru Tokyo Roki / black oil filter with correct 23 PSI bypass valve.

title: Intake Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 2)
meaning: ECM detected the Bank 2 (driver side) intake camshaft remained mechanically advanced beyond commanded position.
symptoms: Check Engine Light illuminated
Flashing Cruise light, Traction Control light illuminated
Engine stumble or rough idle
inspectionSteps: Check oil level on dipstick.
Inspect Bank 2 oil feed line banjo bolt screen behind the driver side timing belt / cam cover.
Swap Bank 1 and Bank 2 OCV solenoids: if code shifts from P0021 to P0011, the solenoid valve plunger is sticky.
verifiedFixes: Remove clogged mesh screen from Bank 2 AVCS oil feed banjo bolt.
Replace Bank 2 AVCS Oil Control Valve (OCV) solenoid with genuine OEM Subaru part.
Change oil with high-detergent synthetic 5W-30 or 0W-20.

title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
meaning: Active Valve Lift System (AVLS) oil pressure switch on Bank 1 cylinder head did not change state when variable valve lift was engaged.
symptoms: Check Engine Light on
Engine surges slightly around 2,500-3,000 RPM
Cruise Control disabled
inspectionSteps: Locate AVLS oil pressure switch and variable valve lift solenoid on Bank 1 rear cylinder head.
Inspect switch connector for engine oil leaking through the plastic housing into the connector pins.
Test continuity of oil pressure switch.
verifiedFixes: Replace AVLS oil pressure diagnostic switch (OEM Subaru 25240AA060) and sealing washer.
Change engine oil with clean 5W-30 or 0W-20.

title: Fuel System Too Lean (Bank 1)
meaning: Total fuel trim (STFT + LTFT) exceeded +25% rich correction threshold due to vacuum leak or low fuel delivery.
symptoms: Engine hesitation on throttle tip-in
Rough idle or surging at stoplights
Check Engine Light on
inspectionSteps: On turbocharged models (WRX / XT / GT): inspect the silicone/rubber turbo inlet pipe where it connects to the turbocharger compressor inlet. The underside tears beneath the hose clamp!
Clean Denso Mass Air Flow (MAF) sensor wires with MAF cleaner spray.
Inspect PCV valve and blue tee connector hoses under intake manifold for hardening, cracks, or blow-off under boost.
verifiedFixes: Replace torn turbo inlet pipe with reinforced silicone inlet pipe.
Clean or replace Denso MAF sensor.
Replace hardened or split PCV vacuum hoses.

title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1)
meaning: ECM detected open circuit, short circuit, or erratic voltage baseline from the piezoelectric knock sensor mounted on top of the Boxer engine block.
symptoms: Severe sluggishness / hesitation under acceleration (ECM defaults to maximum fail-safe ignition timing retard)
Check Engine Light illuminated
Poor fuel economy
inspectionSteps: Locate knock sensor on top of engine block near cylinder #4 (under the throttle body / intake manifold runner).
Inspect plastic body of sensor: engine heat cycles bake the black plastic casing until it cracks, allowing moisture to short out the piezoelectric crystal.
Measure resistance across sensor pin and engine ground (normal is ~560k ohms; open circuit or under 100k ohms indicates sensor failure).
Inspect wiring pigtail for rodent damage.
verifiedFixes: Replace knock sensor with genuine OEM Subaru knock sensor (OEM 22060AA070).
Scrape / clean aluminum corrosion on engine block mounting pad with scotch-brite pad to ensure clean electrical ground.
Torque sensor mounting bolt precisely to 17.4 lb-ft (23.5 Nm) at a 45° angle to the engine centerline (critical for proper acoustic vibration harmonics).

title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
meaning: Rear heated O2 sensor voltage fluctuates in tandem with front wideband A/F sensor, indicating catalytic converter oxygen storage depletion.
symptoms: Check Engine Light illuminated
Flashing Cruise Control light
Fails state emissions inspection
inspectionSteps: Inspect exhaust header donut gaskets: Subaru Boxer unequal and equal length headers flex significantly; leaking header flange gaskets suck in false oxygen, tripping false P0420 codes!
Monitor rear downstream O2 sensor voltage during highway cruise: should stay steady between 0.6V and 0.8V.
Check for oil burning (valve stem seals or PCV valve).
verifiedFixes: Replace exhaust manifold donut gaskets and spring bolts (very common source of false P0420 on Outback/Forester).
Replace downstream secondary heated oxygen sensor (Denso OEM 22690AA831 / 22690AA97A).
Replace catalytic converter pipe assembly with CARB/OEM compliant unit.

title: Transmission Control System (MIL Request)
meaning: Engine Control Module (ECM 7E0) received a request from the Transmission Control Module (TCM 7E1) to illuminate the Check Engine Light due to an active transmission trouble code.
symptoms: Check Engine Light illuminated
Flashing AT OIL TEMP light or flashing Cruise Control light
inspectionSteps: Do NOT clear ECM code without scanning TCM. P0700 contains zero diagnostic fault information on its own.
Use OBD-Hero Multi-ECU Scanner to scan TCM (7E1) directly for the primary fault (common: P2764, P0711, P0971, P2762).
verifiedFixes: Read and repair primary trouble code stored in TCM.
Clear trouble codes across both ECM and TCM computers.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
meaning: ECM detected that the secondary air injection switching valve remained open after the cold-start warm-up cycle completed, allowing exhaust gases back into the air pump circuit.
symptoms: Check Engine Light illuminated
Cruise Control disabled and flashing
Loud hissing or exhaust flutter noise on cold start
inspectionSteps: Locate secondary air combination valves behind cylinder heads / intake manifold.
Inspect air lines for moisture or condensation (water condenses in valves and corrodes internal steel reeds).
Check pressure sensor voltage on Bank 1 valve.
verifiedFixes: Replace Bank 1 secondary air combination valve (OEM Subaru 14864AA020) and install new pipe gaskets.
Blow out secondary air feed hoses to remove trapped condensation.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On
meaning: Pressure sensor detected elevated air pressure in injection rail while the air pump was commanded OFF, or air pump relay contacts welded shut.
symptoms: High-pitched vacuum motor whine running continuously under front driver bumper / fender area
Check Engine Light on
inspectionSteps: Inspect secondary air pump relay in main underhood fuse box (relay contacts frequently melt/weld together under sustained high amperage).
Disconnect air pump connector behind driver headlight: check for water intrusion inside pump housing.
verifiedFixes: Replace secondary air pump relay in fuse box.
Replace secondary air pump motor assembly if internal motor bearing seized or drowned in water.

title: Lock-Up Duty Solenoid Circuit Low (Lineartronic CVT Valve Body)
meaning: Transmission Control Module (TCM) detected an open circuit or high resistance in the torque converter clutch lock-up duty solenoid on the Lineartronic CVT control valve body.
symptoms: "AT OIL TEMP" warning light flashing on instrument cluster
Check Engine Light on, Cruise Control flashing, Hill Start Assist disabled
Vehicle shudders or stalls when coming to a complete stop (converter fails to unlock)
inspectionSteps: Do NOT replace the entire transmission! Over 95% of P2764 codes are caused by a failed 0-20 solenoid coil on top of the valve body.

Disconnect transmission 16-pin harness connector on top of transmission bellhousing and measure resistance across lock-up solenoid pins (normal is 11.0 to 13.5 ohms; open circuit/infinite ohms confirms blown solenoid coil).
Remove top or bottom transmission oil pan (depending on TR580 vs TR690 generation) to access valve body.
verifiedFixes: Replace the torque converter lockup solenoid (resistance ~12 ohms) on the CVT valve body, or replace the rebuilt valve body assembly (Subaru 31706AA034 / 31706AA031).
Drain and refill CVT with genuine Subaru High Torque CVT Fluid (Orange) or Lineartronic II Fluid (Green/Blue) following strict temperature-fill procedure (35°C-45°C).
Perform CVT TCM re-learn / calibration sequence using diagnostic tool.
